NUTRITION FOR TEAM SPORTS

Whether it’s the soccer, hockey, lacrosse, tennis, or football team, when
groups of athletes get together, they can easily end up at pregame tailgate
parties and postgame celebrations that don’t quite fit into an optimal sports
diet. Add in travel, tournaments, and disrupted sleep, and nutrition can
easily fall by the wayside. Yet, with strong leadership from their captains
and coaches, teams can indeed win with good nutrition—especially if they
are competing against teams with suboptimal fueling practices—when
they make a commitment to each other to plan ahead and eat responsibly
and, if the athletes are of drinking age, knock off the alcohol until the end
of the season.

Here are a few factors to consider for teams that want to get to the
winner's circle (Holway and Spriet 2011):

* Most team sports are stop-and-go sports; they involve bursts of
high-intensity play followed by pauses with low activity. Athletes in these
demanding sports can easily become glycogen depleted and dehydrated.
Hence, all athletes need to be responsible and make the effort to fuel
themselves optimally.

© Even with home games, someone needs to plan for food and fluids
before, during, and after games or tournaments, as well as at half-time.
